messages.text: I found a dependency boundary that blocks a safe RQL integration in this lane: the reusable local-transfer logic is embedded in the policy provider, and the policy crate already depends on RQL. The plan also assigns provider work on this seam to another session. I’ll hand this back for coordination before editing that shared file.

I found a crate boundary that needs coordination: RQL cannot use the policy-only composition provider, and the plan assigns provider work on this seam to another session. I handed the parent the relevant code paths and the ownership decision needed before implementation. No files changed or tests ran.
I’ll fetch #8980 and map each provider method before moving code. I’ll flag any method whose inputs come from policy data and send the split map before editing.

I sent the parent the method-by-method split map and stopped at the policy-only model selection that affects dispatch and caller completeness. I also reported that the sandbox blocked `git fetch` and GitHub was unreachable, so I could not obtain #8980’s head. No files changed.
I’ll continue from the merged #8980 base. I’ll check its new hooks first, then split the provider with a required call-model trait and keep the execution hooks intact.

The move reaches a second policy-only input inside snapshot access: `PolicyDiscoveryProvider` owns the cached reads that the neutral provider would need. I’m stopping at that method as requested and will send the parent the exact dependency and a way to preserve read replay.

The provider split exposed a policy-owned discovery cache that supplies snapshot and dispatch reads, including read replay on memo hits. I sent the parent the dependency and a proposed injected discovery trait, then stopped at that contract choice as instructed. No files changed.

I’ll use the approved injected discovery trait and keep policy’s cache in place. I’ll move the shared algorithms first, wire policy through the neutral provider, then add the RQL client and compare answers.

The first shared piece is in place: call-site matching and fallback port selection now live in the flow crate, and policy calls those functions. I’m compiling policy before moving more code so this mechanical change has a clear check.

The policy compile is still working through dependencies. I’ve confirmed that the RQL discovery side can use `WorkspaceValueFlowProvider`’s snapshot and dispatch replay, while policy keeps its existing cache. The remaining extraction is the provider’s larger dispatch, caller, and openness logic.
The compile remains on the semantic and store crates. I’m keeping the current edit small until it finishes, then I’ll address any compiler or lint findings before continuing the split.

Call binding projection has also moved into the shared flow module. That includes the port mapping used by dispatch candidates, so policy now calls the shared function. I’m checking the build before extracting more.

The build found one remaining policy call to the moved `result_port` helper. I updated it to use the shared function and started a repeat check. The provider split and RQL routing are still unfinished.

The shared module now also owns dispatch completeness classification. Policy uses it to decide whether a raw dispatch closes a boundary. I’m validating that move, then I’ll work on the injected discovery interface needed for the larger extraction.

I found and corrected a behavior change in the extracted fallback helper: a missing call row must still return policy’s semantic-unavailable error. The helper now receives the validated row, so that error path remains in policy. I’m running the compile again.

The shared discovery trait now compiles with policy’s existing cache implementation, and the moved helpers compile through policy. The larger neutral provider and RQL client still need implementation. I’m running the requested lint gate on the changed crates to catch issues in this checkpoint.

Clippy is still checking the dependency graph; it has not reported an error yet. The extracted helpers and discovery trait are a compile-clean checkpoint, but the requested RQL result path and equivalence golden are not present yet.

The provider split is incomplete. I moved four label-free helpers into the flow crate and added the discovery trait; policy compile, clippy, formatting, and pack drift checks pass. The neutral provider, RQL client, equivalence golden, and full requested validation remain unfinished. I reported the checkpoint and log paths to the parent.

I’ll take the next compiling step from 73c18e92e4: move the baseline partial-flow read and projection into a neutral provider component, then keep policy’s barrier override delegating to it. I’ll validate that step before changing dispatch or callers.

The procedure lookup has moved from the taint provider into its injected discovery implementation, and policy compiles with the same cache path. Next I’m moving the baseline stored-read and file-local projection code into flow while preserving policy’s counters and barrier branch.

The neutral flow code now performs published partial-flow reads and file-local reprojection through the injected discovery trait. Policy still owns the barrier override and its existing work counters. The compile is running; after it passes I’ll check for unused imports and keep this as a clean checkpoint.

Checkpoint: policy compiles with neutral partial-flow reads and reprojection, plus the required `CallModelSource` trait. The policy implementation preserves its store-end override and caller-model check. I’m moving raw dispatch and candidate binding into the neutral provider next.

Checkpoint: raw dispatch resolution, per-arm binding, and coverage assembly now live in flow; policy supplies model decisions through the required trait. Policy compiles. I found the existing cross-batch memo hit path does not replay dispatch reads, so I’m adding that replay before validating the composition cases.

Checkpoint: neutral dispatch and reverse-caller enumeration now compile through `LocalTransferDiscovery` and `CallModelSource`. Policy still keeps its own memo and diagnostics. The next extraction is openness and interior-flow projection; I’m validating this checkpoint against composition tests before moving either.

The checkpoint is formatted and the focused composition golden build is running. The suite’s caller and call-port cases will check that the moved dispatch and reverse-caller code keeps their rendered answers unchanged.

The focused golden build is still compiling the measure profile, with no test failure reported yet. The source tree remains compile clean and formatted. I’ll wait for the test result, then hand the parent a compiling checkpoint within this turn.

The measure-profile build has reached the flow and language-analysis crates. No failures have appeared. Once the focused tests finish, I’ll report their exact selection and result so the parent can checkpoint this code without assuming a broader suite passed.
The focused test build has reached policy, runtime, and MCP. The tree is still at the same compile-clean checkpoint; I’m waiting for the two selected golden cases to execute before handing it back.

The two selected composition goldens passed byte-for-byte: caller prefetch across worker counts and call-port projection. I’m running clippy on the touched crates, then I’ll hand back this checkpoint for the parent’s commit.

Checkpoint validation passed: policy compiles, clippy is clean across flow/RQL/policy, formatting is clean, and three focused composition tests pass. I’m handing back the compile-clean provider split now; openness, interior projection, and the RQL client remain for the next step.

I handed back a compile-clean checkpoint: shared partial-flow, dispatch, and caller logic now delegates through the approved traits. Policy compile, clippy, formatting, and three focused composition tests pass. The remaining provider split and RQL client are still in progress.
I’ll pick up from the pushed checkpoint and move the remaining shared algorithms first. I’ll verify each step compiles before starting the RQL client.

The shared snapshot status, openness sweep, and refinement-call selection now compile in `bifrost-flow`; policy delegates those reads to it. I’m moving the openness decision next, then checking the policy goldens before extracting interior projection.

The openness decision now lives in the shared module, with policy supplying its memoized partial-flow and dispatch answers. The crate check passed; I’m running clippy and the focused policy goldens to catch any behavior drift.
Clippy passed for flow, policy, and RQL. The focused policy golden build is still running; once it finishes, I’ll check the diff and hand back this compiling checkpoint for the parent’s commit.

The two composition goldens pass byte for byte with a per-run writable cache. The first run failed because the sandbox’s default cache was read-only, so I’m keeping that cache setting for the remaining tests. I’m extracting the shared interior projection now, with policy retaining the barrier fixpoint hook.

The interior projection now runs through a shared algorithm, while policy still chooses and records its barrier filtered fixpoint. The crate check passed. Clippy found only argument-count lint on the extracted interface; I’ve addressed that and am rerunning validation.

The interior extraction compiles and clippy passes. Its policy hook keeps the existing barrier behavior and profiling counters; I’m waiting for the rebuilt composition goldens before handing this checkpoint back.

This checkpoint is compiling and the focused composition goldens remain byte equal. I’m handing it back for the parent’s commit; the RQL client, forced-engine golden, and full gates are the next step.

The shared openness and interior projection changes compile, pass clippy and formatting, and keep the focused policy goldens byte equal. I handed the uncommitted checkpoint and test logs to the parent. RQL integration and full validation remain.

I’ll connect RQL to the shared search from the new checkpoint, starting with the plan’s admission rules and the provider interfaces. I’ll keep the existing ICFG path for features whose result contract the composed client cannot yet express.

The shared search now has a compiling unit-fact entry point for a registered value-flow plan. I found plan features that require explicit admission checks before RQL can call it: conditional sources, dispatch obligations, authored transfer rules, models, and location or kill behavior. I’m keeping the wrapper disconnected until those checks and the provider are in place.
The unit-fact search entry point compiles and passes clippy. I handed the checkpoint to the parent. RQL remains on ICFG until the admission checks, provider, and endpoint mapping are complete.
I’ll add the conservative admission gate first, then wire the RQL provider through it. Any plan feature the composed search cannot represent will keep using ICFG with a recorded reason.

Admission now returns typed reasons for unsupported endpoint conditions, models, location behavior, kills, and authored relations. Ordinary snapshot-derived local and call rules remain eligible because the shared provider reconstructs those transfers. I’m checking the gate’s compile and lint results.
The typed admission gate compiles and passes clippy. I’m handing back this checkpoint; the RQL provider, endpoint mapping, forced-engine golden, and full validation are still outstanding.
The typed admission gate compiles and passes clippy. I handed the checkpoint to the parent; RQL integration and the required golden and full validation remain.

The query-local discovery and unit-fact composition provider compile, and the focused policy goldens pass. I found a contract decision before wiring endpoint rows: a reached endpoint’s current public ID hashes ICFG-only meeting and fact details that the composed search does not produce. I’ll hand the exact dependency and options to the parent.

The shared RQL provider compiles and the focused policy goldens remain byte equal. I handed the parent a decision on reached endpoint IDs: their current format depends on ICFG data the composed search does not produce. RQL wiring is paused pending that contract decision.
I’ll check whether the ICFG path can emit multiple rows for one source and sink before changing reached IDs. Then I’ll use one engine-neutral ID on both paths and audit the golden changes.

The ICFG code can emit multiple reached rows for one source and sink through different summary entries, although the existing golden shows no such duplicate. I handed the parent the evidence and a recommendation to merge those alternative paths before changing the public ID.
I’ll trace where reached endpoint IDs are used and persisted, then send the parent the file and line list before editing that behavior.
I sent the parent the file and line trace for RQL row keys, joins, deduplication, witnesses, persisted policy units, retained evaluations, and goldens. No ID or persisted behavior changed.

I’ll implement the pair aggregate around the existing meeting handles and make its public ID depend on the registered plan and full event identities. I’ll first inspect the plan identity API and witness path so the merge preserves each alternative’s reconstruction owner.

The ICFG path now groups alternative meetings by source and sink before producing rows, while each alternative retains its own witness owner. I’ve added endpoint evidence merging at the later pipeline union and intersection seams. I’m compiling that combined change now.
The neutral ID and pair aggregation compile. I’ve removed the old meeting-based ID helper and am checking clippy across the affected crates before running the value-flow golden.

The Java value-flow golden is still rebuilding its test binary. The new ID uses the registration’s full plan digest and both event identities; witness IDs remain tied to the aggregate endpoint and a unique alternative index. I’ll review the golden result before wiring composition.

The Java value-flow golden passes with the pair merge, and the tree compiles. I found an identity blocker before freezing it: the registration digest I used hashes a procedure handle that includes an allocation pointer, so equivalent plans in separate processes could get different public IDs. I’m sending the parent that evidence and a proposed stable digest boundary.

The pair aggregate compiles and the Java value-flow golden passes. I paused before committing the ID change: its current plan digest includes an allocation pointer, which would make persisted public IDs unstable across processes. I sent the parent the evidence and a stable fingerprint proposal.
I’ll add the stable plan fingerprint and check where the existing registration digest reaches public IDs. Then I’ll continue the endpoint merge and composition wiring.

Master’s reached ID does not use the registration digest. It hashes meeting details, so the allocation-sensitive digest entered public identity only in this lane’s uncommitted change. I’m replacing that use with a fingerprint built from the plan’s stable inputs.

The fingerprint now uses durable procedure keys and stable carrier keys, and RQL no longer feeds the registration digest into reached IDs. RQL checks; the separate-materialization test is still building.
The fingerprint test is still compiling dependencies. I’ll keep the checkout unchanged until that build finishes, then fix any test or formatting failures and continue the RQL engine selection.
The flow test build has reached the flow crate. Once it exits, I’ll run the test by its full name; this first invocation used `--exact` with only the short name.

The first test compared two separate temporary workspaces; their artifact keys differ, so different fingerprints were correct. I changed it to compare separate plan allocations under the same artifact key, then ran formatting.
The fingerprint test is rebuilding the flow test binary after formatting. The earlier RQL library check passed; I’m waiting for the actual test result before treating this checkpoint as verified.

evidence.user_prompt_tail: Parent: approved. Add an explicit stable public plan fingerprint in bifrost-flow, built from durable artifact and procedure keys and every immutable semantic plan input (no handle, pointer or dense solver ID), and use it for reached IDs; the pointer-bearing registration digest stays for allocation validation only, with a comment saying it must not reach a public or persisted identity. Add a debug assertion or test that two separately built registrations of the same plan in one process (different allocations) give the same fingerprint. Also check: does master's current reached ID (or any other public or persisted ID) already include ValueFlowPlanRegistration::plan_digest? If so, master's IDs vary across processes, which is a defect of its own: tell me the sites so I can record it, and this change fixes them. Then finish ordering and idempotence, the product golden with explicit ID checks, the composition mapping and admission, and the gates. Checkpoint note when a turn is ending.
